issues.legal_issue: A civil court cannot determine an objection to compensation for compulsorily acquired land through an ordinary suit when the required reference has not been made.
material_facts: Land was compulsorily acquired, and the claimant accepted the compensation under protest.
The claimant made a written application objecting to the compensation within the prescribed period, but the Collector did not make a reference to the court.
The claimant instead brought an ordinary civil suit, and the civil court granted increased compensation; the appellate court upheld that decree.
The local arrangement allowed the same officers to act on executive and civil sides, but the required reference procedure was not followed.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had no jurisdiction to determine the compensation objection through the suit, and the judgments and decrees were set aside as nullities.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11, 18, 19 and 20 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a timely written application specifying an objection is required for a reference, and a valid reference with the prescribed written statement is a prerequisite to the court taking up the objection. Sections 26 and 54 prescribe the resulting award and appeal process, while Section 3(d) recognizes the relevant court. The special procedure impliedly excludes ordinary civil-court jurisdiction under Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, over such compensation objections. The local provision permitting necessary modifications to the Act did not displace the mandatory reference procedure. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute concerns compensation for land compulsorily acquired.
predicates.ordinary_civil_suit_for_compensation: The claimant brought an ordinary civil suit seeking determination of the compensation objection.
predicates.collector_made_no_formal_reference: The Collector did not formally refer the compensation objection to the court.

issues.definition: When a compensation dispute arising from compulsory acquisition is brought as an ordinary civil suit without a formal reference by the Collector, the civil court lacks jurisdiction to determine the objection.

issues.legal_issue: A Collector must refer a timely written compensation objection to the court when the claimant has made the required application but the Collector has failed to refer it.
material_facts: The claimant submitted a written application objecting to the compensation within the prescribed period and with the requisite particulars.
The Collector did not make the reference, and the court found that the application satisfied the relevant requirements.
The Supreme Court directed the Collector to make the reference for determination by the civil court.
issues.conclusion: The Collector was directed to refer the claimant's objection to the civil court for determination.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 19 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, require a timely written application identifying the objection and a reference accompanied by the prescribed written statement; the reference is a prerequisite to the court proceeding under Section 20. Because the claimant's written application was timely and contained the requisite particulars, the Collector was directed to make the reference. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: acquisition_reference_request and written_request_with_objections and request_made_within_required_period and collector_failed_to_refer

predicates.acquisition_reference_request: A claimant seeks a court determination of an objection concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.written_request_with_objections: The claimant submitted a written request stating the compensation objection and the requisite particulars.
predicates.request_made_within_required_period: The claimant submitted the written request within the applicable period.
predicates.collector_failed_to_refer: The Collector did not refer the claimant's objection to the court.

issues.definition: When a claimant makes a timely written request with the requisite compensation objection and the Collector fails to refer it, the Collector must refer the objection to the court.
